title: 22.	CA BREAST IN PREGNANCY AND PREGNANCY FOLLOWING CA BREAST

blocks.content:
22. CA BREAST IN PREGNANCY AND PREGNANCY FOLLOWING CA BREAST
•1 in 9 women has life time risk.
•Most common female cancer.
•Leading cause of death in between age 35 – 54 years.
•15% diagnosed before 45 years.
•10 – 20% cases associated with pregnancy or occur within 1 years after birth.
•5 Years survival 80% <50 years of age.

CA Breast Diagnosed During Pregnancy:

•Pregnancy itself don’t worse prognosis
•Feeling of lump => refer to Breast specialist.
•Testing in conjunction with MDT team.
•Diagnosis:
1.USG – 1st line.
2.Mammography:
-If cancer is confirmed, to assess the extent with shield.
3.Tissue Biopsy:
-Not cytology because it is inconclusive in pregnancy due to normal proliferative changes.
-H/P, receptor status, stage, Grade.
4.X – RAY chest and spine (bone involvement).
5.liver USG – if needed.
6.MRI with Gadolinium: done only if clinical concerns limited data on safety.
7.Tumor makers – Not recommended – As they are misleading (CA 15-3, CA -125).
8.CT, pelvic x - ray, NR as they have effect on baby.

TOP: MDT review.

Treatment: MDT.

Surgical:

•Wide local excision.
•Sentinel node biopsy, if pre -op USG and needle biopsy has negative results then do S.N Biopsy.
•Avoid blue dye.
•S.N biopsy => positive => axillary clearance.
•MRM.
•Reconstruction is delayed till delivery.

Radio:

•C/I routinely.
•If preservation of organ function is required like spinal cord compression by radio, then do with shield or after Iatrogenic delivery of baby.

 

Chemo:

•C/I – 1st can be given in 2nd and 3rd .
•Anthracyclines safe in pregnancy
-Left ventricular dysfunction.
-Cardiomyopathy.

 

No evidence of

- 2nd miscarriage

- IUGR.

- long Term effect

•5HT3, Steroids => for emesis
•Tamoxifen and trastuzumab (HER 2 new) contraindicated in pregnancy and lactation.

Birth:

•MDT.
•Postpone delivery 2 – 3weeks after last chemo to avoid neutropenic crises.

Lactation:

•B.F on chemo is C/I – as it causes leukopenia & infection in neonates.
•Otherwise offered short duration in between chemo (14days after chemo).

CC:

•Avoid hormonal CC => consider after 5 years free of recurrence.

Pregnancy Following CA – Breast:

<10% became pregnant following diagnosis of CA Breast:

Pre pregnancy:

•Consult:
-Oncologist.
-Surgeon.
-Obstetrician

Stop tamoxifen 3m0 before (washout period) long half-life.

•CA with Mets => Avoid pregnancy as life expectancy is limited and treatment is compromised.
•Pregnancy don’t adversely affect long term survival.
•Avoid pregnancy till 2 years after treatment (highest time for recurrence).
•Outcome of pregnancy after CA Breast No evidence available
•Recommended tamoxifen treatment for CA Breast is 5 years.
•Ed risk of C/section.
•BRCA carrier => PGD.

ANC:

•MDT.
•Echo if risk of cardiomyopathy (on anthracycline, taxanes rare complication).

PNC:

•B.F – from unaffected side.
•Breast conserving surgery – don’t affect milk production from affected side.
•Radio cause fibrosis – lactation not possible.

Effect of treatment on Fertility:

•Discuss with all women, written information.

Chemo:

gonadtoxicity esp. alkylating agents.

•Taxanes less gonadotoxic.
•CMF (Cyclophosphamide, Metho, 5Floro)

=> higher risk of amenorrhea.

•FEC (5floro, epirubicin, cyclophosphamide) =>less amenorrhea
•Tamoxifen => Menstrual irregularity, Endometrial hyperplasia

 

 

Amenorrhea after chemo:

-<30 years = 5%.
-36 – 40 years = 50%.

Fertility preservation Before treatment:

Cryopreservation:

•Egg or Embryo freezing.
•Egg preservation for those with no partners otherwise embryo.
•Embryo preservation success 20%.
•Ovarian stimulation with tamoxifen or letrozole combined with gonadotrophins.
•Ovarian tissue storage => research setting.

ART after Treatment of CA Breast:

•Loss of ovarian reserve due to treatment (chemo).

IVF => estrogenic state.

Egg donation if ovarian failure due to treatment.

Surrogacy – where pregnancy is C/I
